aspect: Unpredictability is the mechanism, not a side effect
description: The value of a flying checkpoint is precisely that you cannot know where it will be. It converts the whole road network into a probabilistic system.

aspect: It lands hardest on anything with a fixed time
description: Dialysis, chemotherapy, an exam, a shift, a wedding, a court date, labour. Anything that cannot be rescheduled is the thing most exposed.
energy_note: The appointments you cannot move are the ones it hits.

description: There is no published standard, no service time, no complaint route and no name. Two 19-year-olds decide how long several hundred people wait.
energy_note: An unappealable decision made by a teenager.

description: She has a job interview in Ramallah at eleven. At 09:20 a jeep parks across the road outside Sinjil. At 11:40 she calls to explain and is told, politely, that they have already seen the other candidates.
money_note: A year of the salary not earned.
energy_note: Losing a job to a parked vehicle.

aspect: Employers learn to price it in, and stop hiring
description: An employer who needs reliable attendance eventually prefers the applicant who does not cross a checkpoint to get to work. The restriction becomes a hiring criterion that nobody ever states.
energy_note: Unemployable because of where you sleep.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the gate that is counted but not staffed
description: OCHA's December 2025 breakdown lists 232 road gates, 159 of them frequently closed, and 218 partial checkpoints of which 152 have gates - 90 usually open, 62 frequently closed. A gate needs no soldier, so closure costs the army nothing and cannot be anticipated by the driver.
energy_note: Three hundred and eighty-four gates, and no timetable for any of them.
